issues.display_title: Issue #1794: [Editor] Polish the Edit Frame dialog: opening flash, spacing, dividers and hover states
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The Edit Frame dialog (Artwork → frame icon) has a handful of rough edges that add up to a window that doesn't feel finished.

What you see:

  • Opening the dialog — before the content shows up, a thin white bar the width of the dialog slides in, then snaps to full size. It looks like something failed to load.
  • Between the two halves — the preview on the left and the settings on the right sit on the old page grid, and the space between them is patched together from paddings and negative margins. Hard to keep even, easy to knock out of line.
  • Bottom of the settings panel — the last part of the panel looks sheared off, most obviously under the colour picker when it's open.
  • Above the footer — two horizontal lines a few pixels apart, one slightly shorter than the other.
  • Save This Frame — sits on the same row as Done instead of next to the "Apply to all Artworks" checkbox, the way the original design had it.
  • The colour picker card — its shadow spreads out on every side and reads as a grey blob rather than the card being lifted off the panel.
  • Preview canvas — square corners, while everything around it in the dialog is rounded.
  • Saved frames, on hover — the thumbnail goes pale instead of dimming, and the two round buttons on top of it are hard to read: the edit one turns into a solid black disc and the icons are too big for the circles they sit in.
  • Save Frame popup — the "Frame Name" box is a grey fill with no border and no reaction when you hover or click into it, unlike every other input in the editor.

What it should look like

The dialog opens at its real size, straight into the content. Two evenly spaced halves, one divider above the footer, rounded preview, and hover states you can actually read. The Frame Name box behaves like the rest of the editor's fields.

Scope

  • Have the dialog's content ready before it animates in.
  • Put the two halves on a real grid with one spacing value, and drop the old column classes and the padding tricks that stood in for it.
  • Replace the custom scroll area in the settings panel with plain native scrolling, which is what was cutting off the bottom.
  • One divider above the footer, not two.
  • Move Save This Frame back beside the "Apply to all Artworks" checkbox, Done alone on the row below.
  • Soften the colour picker's shadow to the same recipe the other floating panels use.
  • Round the preview canvas.
  • Saved-frame hover: dim the thumbnail instead of washing it out, make the two buttons legible, size the icons to their circles, mark delete as the destructive one, and give both a visible keyboard focus ring.
  • Frame Name input onto the shared field styling from #1790 — same size as today, only the look changes.

Verification

  • Open Edit Frame a few times: no white bar, no size jump.
  • Scroll the settings panel to the bottom with the colour picker open — nothing cut off.
  • Hover a saved frame: thumbnail dims, both buttons readable, delete reads as destructive; tab to them and the focus ring shows.
  • Open Save Frame: the name box matches the editor's other inputs, same size as before.
  • Check light and dark.

issues.display_title: Issue #1796: [Editor] Size the Crop Image dialog footer buttons like the other polished dialogs
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The Crop Image dialog (any image upload that goes through cropping — splash screen background, cover, avatar) has footer buttons that look like chips next to the 500px-wide cropper above them.

What you see:

  • Delete, Upload New, Continue — all three are 29px tall pills with a 40px radius, while every other dialog polished so far (Edit Frame, #1794) uses one 40px-tall button with the app's radius. Next to the large cropper, they read as small secondary controls rather than the actions of the window.
  • Delete and Continue — each carries a hardcoded pixel width (78px and 113px) from the days when their label had to be padded out. The width no longer matches the label, so the padding inside those two buttons differs from Upload New.

What it should look like

Footer actions the same size and shape as the Edit Frame dialog's: one height, one radius, one weight, labels centred, spacing even between all three.

Scope

  • Give the Crop Image footer the same button geometry Edit Frame already uses, sharing one rule instead of a second copy of it.
  • Drop the hardcoded widths on Delete and Continue — the loading spinner keeps the label in place, so the widths were not holding anything.
  • Even spacing between the buttons.

Verification

  • Open Crop Image from the splash screen background upload: all three buttons the same height and radius as the Edit Frame footer, labels centred.
  • Click Delete and Continue and watch the loading state — the button does not change width.
  • Check light and dark.

issues.display_title: Issue #1797: [Editor] Polish the Edit Splash Screen dialog: note placement, zoom buttons and column padding
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The Edit Splash Screen dialog has three rough edges in the preview column and one in the settings column.

What you see:

  • The "Drag the mobile screen left and right…" note — sits above the preview, so it pushes the preview and its zoom controls down the column. It is also a note about the preview, read before there is anything to read it against.
  • The zoom −/+ buttons — 24px discs on a tinted fill with a border and a muted icon, while the same control in Edit Frame and Field of View is a larger borderless button with a full-strength icon. Three near-identical copies of that style live in three component stylesheets.
  • The settings column — an 18px top padding above the upload box that nothing else in the dialog lines up with.

What it should look like

Preview first, then the zoom row, then the device toggle, then the note. Zoom −/+ identical to Edit Frame's, borderless. Settings column starting flush with the preview.

Scope

  • Move the mobile-drag note below the device toggle.
  • Move the zoom −/+ style into one shared rule and delete the per-component copies in the splash screen, Edit Frame and Field of View.
  • Make that button borderless: transparent ground and border, hover fill only, box size unchanged so nothing shifts.
  • Drop the settings column's top padding.

Verification

  • Open Edit Splash Screen in mobile view: the note reads under the device toggle, and the preview sits at the top of the column.
  • Switch to desktop view: the note hides as before and the layout below it does not move.
  • Zoom −/+ match Edit Frame and Field of View — same size, no border, hover and focus states present in all three.
  • Settings column starts level with the preview.
  • Check light and dark.
